Unit 1 · Real Numbers

ConceptsExamplesExercise

Concepts

Learn the ideas before attempting the exercise.

Real numbers include every number that can be placed on the number line. This section separates them into rational and irrational numbers, then develops the algebraic and order properties used throughout the chapter.

Rational numbers

A real number is rational when it can be written in the form , where and .

Integers are rational because every integer can be written as .

The decimal test

A terminating decimal has finitely many digits after the decimal point. A recurring decimal continues forever but repeats a fixed block.

A real number is rational exactly when its decimal expansion terminates or eventually repeats. A nonterminating, nonrecurring decimal is irrational.

Irrational and real numbers

An irrational number cannot be expressed as a quotient of two integers. Its decimal expansion is nonterminating and nonrecurring.

The real-number set is the union of the rational and irrational numbers.

Perfect-square test

If is a positive integer and is not a perfect square, then is irrational.

Quick check. The nearest perfect squares around are and . Therefore is irrational and lies between and .

Properties of real numbers

Commutative
Associative
Identity
Inverse
Distributive
Cancellation

Order and inequality

Adding the same real number to both sides does not change the direction of an inequality.

Multiplication or division by a positive number keeps the direction. Multiplication or division by a negative number reverses it.

The reciprocal rule requires nonzero numbers on the same side of zero.

Numbers between numbers

Between any two distinct rational numbers there are infinitely many rational numbers. The average gives one immediately.

Repeating the averaging process gives more and more rational numbers.

Historical note

By about , Greek mathematicians knew that the side and diagonal of a square are incommensurable. In modern language, the diagonal of a unit square has length , and is irrational. The exact individual responsible is uncertain.

Further reading: Mathematical Association of America.

Fun fact: a recurring decimal can equal an integer

There is no real number between and ; they are two notations for the same real number.

A note on history

The Pythagorean school in ancient Greece discovered that the diagonal of a unit square is incommensurable with its side, in modern terms, that is irrational. The story that Hippasus was drowned for revealing it is a much later legend and should not be presented as established fact.

06Order properties and inequalities

Definition

The real numbers are ordered: given any two of them, one is smaller, or they are equal.

The rule, with its conditions

Adding never changes the direction. Multiplying or dividing by a negative number always reverses it.

Worked example

Solve .

  1. Subtract from both sides; the direction does not change.
  2. Divide both sides by , a negative number, so reverse the sign.
Answer

Common misconception

Forgetting to reverse

Writing above is the single most common inequality error in this unit. Any time a negative factor is divided out, flip the symbol.

Quick check

If , is always true?

Show the answer

No. It holds only when and have the same sign. For and : .

Did you know?

Density

Between any two distinct real numbers there is another real number, in fact infinitely many rationals and infinitely many irrationals. The number line has no gaps and no smallest step.

Concepts

Learn the ideas before attempting the exercise.

Radicals and indices are two notations for the same operations. This section develops their laws, explains surds and conjugates, and shows why rationalizing a denominator works.

Radicals and the th root

A real number is an th root of when . The principal root is written .

In , is the radicand and is the index. If no index is written, the index is .

For even indices in the real-number system, the radicand must be nonnegative and the principal root is nonnegative.

Laws of radicals

Surds and like terms

A surd is an irrational radical with a rational radicand. Examples include and .

Surds with one term are monomial; expressions such as are binomial surds. Only like surds can be combined by adding coefficients.

Conjugates

The conjugates of and are obtained by changing the sign between the terms.

The middle terms cancel, so the product contains no surd.

Rationalizing the denominator

Multiplying numerator and denominator by the same nonzero expression multiplies the fraction by and does not change its value.

For a binomial denominator, multiply by its conjugate.

  • When rationalizing, multiply both numerator and denominator by the same factor.

Historical note

Ancient Babylonian mathematics contained a remarkably accurate approximation to . Much later, Greek mathematics proved that the diagonal-to-side ratio of a square cannot be a ratio of integers.

02Rationalizing a denominator

Definition

To rationalize a denominator is to rewrite a fraction so that no radical remains below the line, without changing its value.

The rule, with its conditions

Monomial denominator multiply by the surd itself. Binomial denominator multiply by the conjugate.

ConceptsExamplesExercise

Concepts

Learn the ideas before attempting the exercise.

Word problems become manageable when the quantities are named, translated into equations, and checked against the original situation. This section combines linear equations with temperature, percentage, tax, profit, loss, and compound markup.

From words to equations

  1. Name the unknown quantity.
  2. Translate each condition into an equation.
  3. Solve one step at a time.
  4. Substitute the answer back into the original conditions.
Example. If two numbers have sum and difference , write and .

Temperature conversion

The school text rounds to in its exercises. Scientific work normally uses .

Reference: NIST temperature conversions.

Percent means “per hundred”

To find of a quantity , calculate .

Profit and loss

The denominator is the cost price because profit or loss is measured relative to what was originally paid.

Simple profit, tax, and ratios

In , use the rate as a decimal and time in years. For ratio sharing, add the ratio parts first, find one part, then multiply.

Compound markup

Here is principal, is the annual rate in decimal form, is the number of compounding periods per year, and is time in years.

Check before accepting an answer

  • A selling price with profit should exceed the cost price.
  • A loss percentage should be positive and below in ordinary cases.
  • A Fahrenheit temperature corresponding to a hot Celsius temperature should be larger numerically.
  • Ages, lengths, money, and counts must use appropriate units.
